== Biography ==
Following support from the Landesgraduiertenförderung, Baden-Württemberg (Scholarship)<ref name=":1" /> and Graduiertenkolleg Heidelberg (Scholarship),<ref>{{Cite web|title=Graduiertenförderung|url=https://mwk.baden-wuerttemberg.de/de/forschung/forschungsfoerderung/wissenschaftlicher-nachwuchs/graduiertenfoerderung/|access-date=2021-03-28|website=Baden-Württemberg.de|language=de}}</ref> Buchmueller received his doctorate from [[Heidelberg University]] in 1999. From 1999 to 2001 he was a CERN fellow at the ALEPH Experiment studying properties of the Z and W Bosons and in 2001 he joined SLAC as a research associate to work on the BABAR experiment.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Graduiertenförderung|url=https://mwk.baden-wuerttemberg.de/de/forschung/forschungsfoerderung/wissenschaftlicher-nachwuchs/graduiertenfoerderung/|access-date=2021-03-31|website=Baden-Württemberg.de|language=de}}</ref> He returned to CERN in 2004 as research staff member of the organization making important contributions to the construction, commissioning, and physics exploitation of the CMS experiment.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/970621|title=Proceedings of the first LHC Detector AlignmentWorkshop: CERN, Geneva, Switzerland 4 - 6 Sep 2006|date=2007|publisher=CERN|isbn=978-92-9083-295-9|editor-last=Blusk|editor-first=S.|series=CERN Yellow Reports: Conference Proceedings|location=Geneva|editor-last2=Buchmüller|editor-first2=Oliver|editor-last3=Jacholkowski|editor-first3=Adam|editor-last4=Ruf|editor-first4=T.|editor-last5=Schieck|editor-first5=Jochen|editor-last6=Viret|editor-first6=S.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Buchmüller|first1=O.|last2=Schilling|first2=F. -P.|date=2007-08-01|title=Status and Commissioning of the CMS Experiment|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0920563207003763|journal=Nuclear Physics B - Proceedings Supplements|series=Proceedings of the 11th International Conference on B-Physics at Hadron Machines|language=en|volume=170|pages=264–272|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysbps.2007.05.029|issn=0920-5632|arxiv=hep-ex/0701019|bibcode=2007NuPhS.170..264B |s2cid=16428738}}</ref> He has been associated with Imperial College of London since 2009 as a professor.

=== CMS Experimentation at CERN ===
Buchmueller joined Compact Muon Solenoid experiment at CERN in 2003. During 2004-2005 he served as the convener of the Tracker alignment group. During 2005-2007 he has been the co-convenor of Calibration and Alignment group. In 2007, he initiated The MasterCode Project along with theoreticians and other scientists with the aim to interpret the data related to LHC results in better fashion.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research - Professor Oliver Buchmueller|url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/o.buchmueller/research.html|access-date=2021-03-25|website=www.imperial.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=MasterCode|url=https://mastercode.web.cern.ch/|access-date=2021-03-25|website=mastercode.web.cern.ch}}</ref> In 2008-2009 he was in charge of the Physics group as co-leader and taking care of researches regarding [[Supersymmetry|supersymmetry (SUSY)]] and later he became the member of the Physics Management Office. He was the chair of CMS analysis review committee while examining the data analysis for developing and overseeing the scientific validity of the key ‘diphoton’ discovery and subsequent characterization channel.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> In September 2016, Buchmueller was nominated as the convener of the EXOTICA search group in CMS.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Fermilab - Fermi Research Alliance|url=https://indico.fnal.gov/event/9353/contributions/114013/attachments/73975/88790/150210_CMS_DOEInstRev.pdf|journal=CMS Program - Kevin Burkett, DOE Institutional Review, February 10, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=CoEPP Annual Report 2015|url=https://issuu.com/coepp/docs/coepp-web-03_4apr_|access-date=2021-03-25|website=Issuu|date=5 April 2016 |language=en}}</ref> He is presently serving as the editor of Supersymmetry (SUSY) related topics at Particle Physics Data Group.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Supersymmetry: post discovery of a new (Higgs?) boson.|url=https://indico.cern.ch/event/201969/|access-date=2021-03-25|website=Indico}}</ref>

=== Atom Interferometer Observatory and Network ===
Buchmueller is presently serving as the Principal Investigator of The Atom Interferometer Observatory and Network where he was appointed in 2018. The network is an inter-university collaborative effort involving [[King's College London]], the [[University of Liverpool]], the [[University of Oxford]], [[University of Birmingham]], the [[University of Cambridge]] and [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory|STFC Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]] while being led by Imperial College of London.<ref name=":1" /> The aim of the project is the exploration of the dark matter and gravitational waves and to ascertain viable options for applying and implementing quantum technology in commercial domain. As Buchmueller said, the network is designed to "harness cold atom technologies" in order to explore fundamental concerns of fundamental physics, astrophysics and cosmology.<ref name="imperial.ac.uk"/><ref name="www2.physics.ox.ac.uk"/> The project received £7.2m funding from [[UK Research and Innovation]] and £2.5m for the involved institutions<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-03-04|title=Quantum sensing for particle physics|url=https://cerncourier.com/a/quantum-sensing-for-particle-physics/|access-date=2021-03-28|website=CERN Courier|language=en-GB}}</ref> in January 2021 for developing the first large-scale atom interferometer in the UK.<ref name="www2.physics.ox.ac.uk"/>
